actual_scope: Exact filtered count and determinant distribution for optimal second callees when P=J_3(lambda), lambda nonzero and lambda^2 != 1, over every finite field.
scope_change_reason: The card proposes a selected-assumption audit. This contribution instead resolves Nicholas Stone PR5556's explicit regular three-dimensional Jordan counting question, as an algebraic side result; no predecessor is audited and no selected assumption is discharged.
bottleneck_link: The retained ordinary wrapper admits many equally rank-optimal second maps. This gives the first exact regular J3 inventory and its determinant fibers, without asserting that any such map has an affordable physical implementation.
stop_rule: Stop after the first verified exact regular J3 count; leave resonance and coupled blocks as open questions.
evidence: PROOF.md gives the all-field rank-one fiber proof. verify.py enumerates every parameter in nine fields, compares full 3x3 matrix domains over F4 and F5, evaluates literal determinants and wrapper columns, and rejects mutations.

open_questions.question: How many optimal second callees exist for P=J_3(lambda) when lambda^2=1?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This completes the missing resonant branch of the same Jordan block.
open_questions.first_step: Use the noninvertible-A quotient characterization in PR5228; distinguish characteristic two from odd characteristic.
open_questions.blocked_by: The proof here requires P^2-I invertible.

open_questions.question: How does the filtered count behave for a first map with multiple Jordan blocks?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Independent single-block counts do not account for off-diagonal square-zero couplings.
open_questions.first_step: Choose two explicitly specified blocks and derive the coupled determinant filter before counting.
open_questions.blocked_by: The square-zero parameter can have rank greater than one and mix the blocks.
